newsitem.title: INDIA: India, Philippines see $500 mln trade by 2000.
newsitem.headline: India, Philippines see $500 mln trade by 2000.

text.p: India and the Philippines agreed on Tuesday to raise their bilateral trade to $500 million by 2000, a Commerce Ministry statement said.

"India and Philippines have agreed to raise the level of bilateral trade to $500 million by the year 2000 to reflect the tremendous potential for trade and economic cooperation between the two countries," the statement said.
The statement was issued after a round of talks between trade officials of the two countries.
Jose Juliano, leader of the Philippines' delegation, said the forthcoming visit of President Fidel Ramos in March was expected to boost bilateral trades.
The two countries would increase cooperation in small and medium enterprises and software development and computers, the statement said.
"Philippines is keen to avail of the Indian expertise in this sector to promote mass computer literacy in the Philippines," it added.
Indian exports to Philippines in 1995/96 were valued at $144.15 million and imports from Philippines amounted to $21.63 million over the same period, the statement said.
Businessmen from the two nations on Tuesday signed agreements on computer training methodology and manufacture and marketing of pharmaceuticals in the Philippines.
